title: Visitor Satisfaction Index for the Sustainable Management of Expo Cebú Chone, Ecuador
content: The purpose of this study is to validate the identified dimensions of visitor satisfaction and assess their potential as indicators of sustainable event management in the context of Expo Cebú Chone 2024 in Ecuador. The research design is quantitative, cross-sectional, and empirical, based on a Likert-scale questionnaire regarding visitor experience and satisfaction. A total of 962 valid responses were collected and analyzed; exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis was applied to 356 of them. The results highlight the two-dimensional nature of satisfaction—across both the event’s main activities and complementary services—grounded in the visitor experience, emphasizing the construct's multidimensionality and its use as an indicator of sustainable event management. It is concluded that the creation of positive experiences constitutes a central component of visitor satisfaction and, in turn, an indirect measure of sustainable event management and the capacity to generate economic, social, and experiential value. This contribution to the literature emphasizes a visitor-centered approach to event sustainability, with practical implications for improving event management in rural livestock-raising areas.
